items.summary: WSJ reports Iran is fortifying its defenses as it braces for potential renewed US strikes after the Nov 3 midterms. Satellite imagery analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security shows dirt mounds and passive barriers built around the Pickaxe Mountain and Natanz nuclear sites to obstruct ground raids; Tehran has used the fighting pause since late July to rebuild missile and drone production. The regime is also rallying the public (billboards advertising shoulder-fired-missile training, IRGC units visiting kindergartens) and has warned regional officials of wider escalation — including possible ground incursions into neighboring countries, strikes on US warships and Saudi oil facilities — if Washington resumes strikes. On the US side, a third carrier strike group and a Marine expeditionary unit are heading to the region while the Pentagon weighs more air defenses for regional bases.
items.title: WSJ: Iran fortifying nuclear sites and rallying public for potential post-midterm US strikes
